title: Cherry and the Lost Puffin
markdown:
Cherry the chinchilla was the softest fluffiest creature you ever did see, like a dandelion puffball with big curious eyes and whiskers that twitched with every little breeze. She lived in a cozy meadow that tickled the edge of the sea. The sea sparkled like a thousand tiny diamonds. Every day was much the same. She’d munch on grass that tasted like honey, take naps in warm sunbeams, and sometimes watch the waves from her favourite smooth grey rock. Peaceful. Familiar. She loved her meadow. It felt safe.

And then there was Reef, a little whale small enough to play in the shallow waves. He loved to peek his blowhole out and say hello to Cherry. All smiles and happy splashes, tail fin a blur. Cherry’s best friend. They spent their days sharing secrets and watching fluffy clouds. Reef’s bubbly laughter was little waves clapping on the shore.

One sunny afternoon, as Cherry nibbled a particularly delicious daisy and Reef did a little happy dance of little waves, something fluttered down from the sky. It landed right between them. Not a leaf. Not a feather. A paper airplane, bright blue and folded very neatly. It looked as if it had travelled a long, long way.

When it landed with a soft thump, Cherry’s whiskers twitched nervously. She tucked her paws under her chin. A stranger. What if they wanted to change things? Her soft fur felt a little less fluffy.

Reef splashed a happy curious greeting, sending little droplets of sea spray. “What is it, Cherry?”

Cherry carefully unfolded the paper with her tiny paws. Wobbly letters, as if written by someone in a hurry: HELP. I’m Pip the puffin, and I’m a little bit lost. I came for a visit to the school, and now I don’t know how to get back to my cozy puffin burrow. My tummy is rumbling. Please can someone help?

Cherry’s whiskers quivered. A lost puffin. A rumbling tummy. A new situation. What if the puffin wasn’t nice? What if the lost place was very, very big? A little flutter started in her chest, like tiny moth wings. What if she couldn’t help? She didn’t like the idea of anyone being hungry.

“Oh dear. Poor Pip. He sounds so sad.”

Reef nudged her gently with his smooth cool head. “We can help. Let’s fold another airplane and send it back. Maybe he’ll see it.”

Cherry giggled, a little nervous. “But Reef, he’s lost. He needs us to go to him. He needs to know where his cozy burrow is.”

Reef’s eyes sparkled. “Yes. An adventure. A puffin rescue.”

An adventure meant going somewhere new. Somewhere she didn’t know. Somewhere she might have to do things she’d never done. But Pip was lost and hungry. She looked at Reef’s excited face, his whole body practically vibrating. Reef never worried. He always made things seem fun. “Okay. Okay, Reef. We’ll go find Pip. We will find the Whispering Woods.”

The paper airplane said Pip might be near the Whispering Woods. Cherry had never been that far from her meadow. A wobble of doubt started in her paws. What if the woods were too shadowy? What if it was too quiet? She felt a familiar urge to just go back to her sunbeam nap.

“Don’t worry, Cherry.” Reef’s voice was like a warm hug. “I’ll be right there. We can cross the Giggle Stream and hop over the Wobbly Bridge. The busy bee in the meadow said the Whispering Woods are just past those. He was buzzing really fast and pointed with one of his little legs.”

So Cherry took a deep breath. With Reef swimming cheerfully beside her along the shoreline, tail flicking, they headed toward the Giggle Stream. A sparkly babbling little river that sounded like a thousand tiny bells. They hopped across on smooth round stones, little feet making soft plink-plink sounds. Easy peasy. Next was the Wobbly Bridge, sturdy vines woven like a friendly hug, swaying just a little in the breeze. Cherry’s little paws felt even wobblier than the bridge. She squeezed her eyes shut, heart going thump-thump-thump. Too wobbly. She might fall. Then she heard Reef’s happy splash on the other side. She opened her eyes. Reef was already there, smile as wide as ever, waving his fin. With a brave little hop, Cherry followed, legs feeling surprisingly steady.

“You did it,” cheered Reef.
“I did.” A tiny spark of bravery.

Soon they reached the edge of the Whispering Woods. It wasn’t shadowy at all. Sunlight dappled through the leaves, golden patterns dancing on the mossy ground. Birds sang cheerful songs. The air smelled like sweet berries and damp earth. Reef pointed his snout toward a clearing.

And there, sitting on a large mossy stone, looking rather glum, was Pip the puffin. Feathers a little ruffled. Bright inquisitive eyes sad. Little puffin sighs. “I was hoping for berries. My tummy is making the loudest noises I’ve ever heard.”

Cherry rushed forward, the wobbly feeling forgotten. “Pip. We got your airplane. We came to help. I’m Cherry, and this is my friend Reef.”

Pip blinked, sad eyes widening. “You did? Oh, thank goodness. I was so hungry I thought I might just float away on an empty tummy.”

The best berries, Pip explained, the sweetest juiciest ones, grew on a tall bush just a little further into the woods, where the sunbeams were warmest. Cherry looked up. The bush was quite tall. The berries were bright red and juicy, plump and inviting. A familiar flutter. What if she fell? She imagined tumbling down among the leaves.

But then she saw Pip’s hopeful face, beak turned toward the berry bush, and Reef nudged her encouragingly. “I’ll get them.” Her voice surprisingly strong.

She took a deep breath, picturing herself climbing carefully, like a little furry mountain goat. She scrambled up the bush, tiny claws gripping the bark. The leaves tickled her nose, smelling wonderfully green. She reached for the ripest reddest berries, little jewels. She gathered them in her paws, little chest puffing with pride. She hesitated, looking at the drop below. A little high. A tiny tremor through her whiskers. What if she dropped them all? Pip would still be hungry. She looked at her favourite smooth grey pebble in her pouch. Warm and familiar. She carefully placed the pebble on a sturdy branch, a little marker, then climbed back down, paws steady and sure.

She landed softly on the moss, a precious pile of the juiciest berries. She offered them to Pip with a big smile. “Here you go.”

Pip’s eyes lit up like little stars. “Thank you. You are so brave and kind, Cherry. And Reef, thank you for bringing her.” He happily pecked at the berries. Soon his tummy stopped rumbling, replaced by happy little chirps. His whole body wiggled with delight.

With Pip fed and happy, they knew it was time to go. They said goodbye at the edge of the woods, promising to visit again soon, maybe bringing a little picnic. Pip waved his little wing. “Thank you for finding me. You saved my tummy.”

As Cherry and Reef made their way back toward their meadow, the sun was beginning to set, painting the sky orange and pink like a giant delicious sherbet. Cherry felt different. The flutter of worry was still there, a tiny whisper, but now it was joined by a warm buzzing hum. She had climbed a tall bush. She had helped a new friend. She had faced the unfamiliar woods and found her way through.

Back in their familiar meadow, Cherry nibbled a blade of grass, and Reef did a gentle splash in the twilight. The meadow still felt cozy and safe. A slightly larger wave splashed a little closer than usual, but Cherry didn’t flinch. She tilted her head, a small confident smile. Her whiskers twitched, not with worry, but with the happy memory of the berry bush, the giggling stream, and the friendly puffin. She felt a warmth spread through her, like she’d swallowed a tiny sunbeam. Tomorrow she might fetch her pebble from the branch. Tonight the meadow was enough, and so was the sea, and so was Reef.
